clue.text: Briefly awkward situation with a bit of a looker

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its final letter

parts.note: to be in a corner is to be in an awkward spot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tricky moment shared with someone rather good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of a looker' sounds like an attractive person, but a looker here is an eye, and the cornea is one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the clear front layer of the eye, so it is literally part of the organ that looks.

clue.text: Person who exposes Kate's error oddly upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, taken as letters

indicators.note: oddly keeps only the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of error

explanation.surface: Someone causes a scandal by revealing Kate's blunder, and is oddly upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The person who exposes something is a STREAKER, who exposes himself at a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker runs naked in public, so he is literally someone who exposes his body.

clue.text: Angry diners getting more sarcastic

indicators.note: angry suggests agitation and turmoil, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Restaurant customers who are cross start making cutting remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snide means sneering and mocking, so the comparative is a synonym for more sarcastic.

clue.text: Granny is taken in by old-time Cockney merchant?

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so these words sit within the outer letters

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Grandma is swindled by an old-fashioned East End trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang uses 'merchant banker' for a rude word for a masturbator; 'merchant' alone is the clipped form, so the question mark marks a definition by slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang a merchant is a vulgar term for one who masturbates, which is exactly what an onanist is.

clue.text: Jug possibly holding 3 flowers?

indicators.note: holding means having something inside, so two of the pieces surround the third

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy, the first of three rivers
the Ure is a Yorkshire river, the second of the three
R is the map abbreviation for river, the third

explanation.surface: A jug that might contain a bunch of three flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Flowers reads as blooms in a vase, but a flower in crosswords is a river, something that flows; three rivers make the answer, with the Ure inside the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: A jug is a vessel for pouring liquids, so it is one example of a pourer.

clue.text: Tailor comes across as outspoken on terrace

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, and on the football terrace in a broad casual accent

parts.note: comes across as means seems to, which a terrace crowd might slur as seems ter

explanation.surface: A tailor makes himself heard among the fans standing on the football terraces.
explanation.walkthrough: Terraces are the standing areas of British football grounds; the casual pronunciation of 'seems to' as 'seems ter' gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamster is a person who sews clothes, a synonym for a tailor.

clue.text: Able to control movement in Europe?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: able to control one's bowels or bladder
second meaning: a large landmass, as Europe is

explanation.surface: Someone or something capable of directing a political movement across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The movement is a bowel movement, not a political one; the question mark flags Europe as an example of the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes control over bodily functions, and the noun names a major landmass such as Europe.

clue.text: Type of poem in small volume

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, here the poem inside the measure

parts.note: ML is the abbreviation for millilitre, a small unit of volume
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A short poem published as a slim book.
explanation.walkthrough: Volume suggests a book, but it is a measure of capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a particular version or kind of a product, so it is a synonym of type.

clue.text: Meaning of clue missing start and finish

indicators.note: missing start says the first letter is dropped from the preceding word

parts.note: a clue is a hint
a finish is an ending

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what a clue means when its first and last bits are lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests losing both ends of one word; in fact only the hint loses its start, and finish is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, so the present participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Vehicle opening for Paul Walker?

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: an opening is the very start of something, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of Paul

explanation.surface: A car with a door held open for Paul Walker, the late Fast and Furious actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Walker reads as a film star's name; Walker is the definition, with a question mark because a tramp is one kind of walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a vagrant who travels on foot, and to tramp is to walk heavily, so a tramp is a walker.

clue.text: Viewer's complaint ends in references about Mary Whitehouse

indicators.note: ends in points to the final letter of each of the following words

parts.note: last letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Mary Whitehouse, the British campaigner against sex and violence on TV, was famous for complaining about what viewers saw.
explanation.walkthrough: A viewer's complaint sounds like a protest letter to the BBC, but the viewer is an eye and the complaint an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an ailment of the organ that views.

clue.text: 4 has time for whiskey in The Ship

indicators.note: has one thing for another means one letter is put in place of another

parts.note: the answer at 4 down has this vulgar slang synonym
T is the abbreviation for time
whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rude so-and-so in a pub called The Ship has time for a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference leads to a vulgar British insult; swapping its first letter W for T gives the ship. The Ship sounds like a pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tanker is a large vessel built to carry oil or other liquid in bulk.

clue.text: World almost consumed in flood

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is left off

parts.note: Saturn is a world, a planet
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: The whole world is nearly engulfed by a great flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed in' looks like a container instruction, but consumed is simply ate and in links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To saturate is to soak something thoroughly, the same as to flood it with liquid.

clue.text: Celebrity dropping E in planetarium?

indicators.note: dropping a letter means letting it fall away from the word

parts.note: a planetarium is a dome where stars are shown, a star dome; the question mark admits the coinage
the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A famous person loses an E in a planetarium.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being a star, which is celebrity or fame.

clue.text: Tutors prepared to admit Oxford University is far from straightforward

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other
prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram material
OU abbreviates Oxford University

explanation.surface: Oxford dons get ready for admissions interviews that are anything but simple.
explanation.walkthrough: The university's abbreviation goes inside the rearranged tutors, not at either end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortuous means full of twists and turns, hence complicated and devious rather than direct.

clue.text: Sound from 11 piece contributing to calypso in Kingston

indicators.note: a piece contributing to something is a part of it, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: letters running across the words

explanation.surface: A noise heard in a calypso song performed in Kingston, Jamaica.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer at 11 is a stye, but read as sty, a pigpen; its sound is a pig's grunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig makes this grunting noise, and pigs live in a sty, the second sense of the word at 11.

clue.text: Senior royal essentially admitting one's out of touch, perhaps

indicators.note: one is put out and the possessive s let in, a swap of one letter for another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: essentially means at its heart, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: middle letter of royal

explanation.surface: An elderly royal concedes that they are rather out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: One is the letter I, which leaves the first word while an S is let in. 'out of touch' reads as one phrase, but out belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensory means relating to the senses, and touch is one of them; the question mark marks touch as just one example.

clue.text: Actor delivered gloss for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so this signals such a swap

parts.note: delivered as in born, and gloss as a sheen; swapping the opening sounds

explanation.surface: An actor gave a line reading with a certain polish, as Spooner would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean is said 'Shawn', so swapping the initial sounds of born and sheen gives 'Shawn Been'. Sean Bean is an English actor known for Game of Thrones.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean Bean is a well-known English film and television actor, so he is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Socialite family entertaining posh doctor

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them in, so the following pieces go inside

parts.note: a clan is a family group
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
BM, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A sociable person's family plays host to an upper-class physician.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the old U and non-U distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubman is a man who frequents gentlemen's clubs, a sociable figure in society.

clue.text: State accepting unfinished Italian resort is deplorable

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so the resort sits inside the state

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Rimini is an Adriatic seaside resort

explanation.surface: An American state taking in a half-built Italian resort is shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal in its informal sense means shocking or disgraceful, as in a criminal waste.

clue.text: Soldiers without indication of fear become submissive

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the soldiers surround the cry

parts.note: men are rank-and-file soldiers
eek is a squeal of fright

explanation.surface: Fearless troops grow meek.
explanation.walkthrough: Without reads as lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To meeken is to make or grow meek, which is to turn gentle and submissive.

clue.text: Price of golf covered by Daily Express leader

indicators.note: covered by means enclosed, so the single letter goes inside the others

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, as is a char
golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so just the initial letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of Express

explanation.surface: The cost of golf as reported in the Daily Express's editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British newspaper, but daily here is a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price asked for goods or a service.

clue.text: Half Man Half Biscuit leading us in refrain

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the earlier pieces come before the last
half means only one of two equal parts is kept

parts.note: a chap is a man
an Oreo is a brand of biscuit
taken as written

explanation.surface: The cult Birkenhead band Half Man Half Biscuit leads us in singing the chorus.
explanation.walkthrough: Half Man Half Biscuit is a British indie band; the name is split so each half takes half a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorus is the part of a song repeated after each verse, the same as a refrain.

clue.text: 8 ogling actress

indicators.note: the answer at 8 used as a verb means to shape or mould, so the next word is reshaped

parts.note: anagram material

explanation.surface: A fashion model eyeing up a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference looks like a noun, a fashion model, but it is a verb: to model clay is to reshape it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong Li is a Chinese film actress, star of Raise the Red Lantern.

clue.text: Great thing that could come before those going my way

definitions.text: thing that could come before those going my way
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a prefix that can sit in front of words for those who travel along a road, as in supertramps

explanation.surface: A cheerful note on something that might precede fellow travellers on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is cryptic: the word works as a prefix, placed before a word for wanderers.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it is informal praise meaning excellent, and as a prefix it attaches before other words.

clue.text: Wild boars with tendency to get thirsty?

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: anagram material
a bent is a natural inclination

explanation.surface: Feral pigs inclined to get dry after rooting about.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark says thirsty is used loosely: something absorbent soaks up liquid, as if thirsty for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent material draws in moisture eagerly, a playful picture of thirst.

clue.text: Person who fools party queen recently

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the queen until 2022

explanation.surface: Someone who tricked the people at a recent gathering for the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Recently signals that ER is the late queen, since the present monarch is CR.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe is to deceive or trick, so a duper is someone who fools others.

clue.text: Sick aunt to recover of course

indicators.note: sick means unwell and out of sorts, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: anagram material
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: An ill aunt will get better, of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and of course are both adverbs meaning as expected or obviously.
